owner_creation.analysis: In src/version.rs, the module defines one four-byte C character array initialized from the exact 712 NUL literal; no allocator or initializer callback creates it.
owner_creation.invariant: Version bytes reside in static storage.

aliases_escapes.analysis: In src/version.rs, the exported version symbol is borrowed by command::dispversion, optfunc::opt__V and lesskey_parse numeric parsing; maintained call sites read its bytes.
aliases_escapes.invariant: C string readers borrow a four-byte NUL string.

callback_targets.analysis: In src/version.rs, the transmute changes the four-byte array element representation only; the module registers no callback or code pointer.
callback_targets.invariant: Array conversion cannot create callback ownership.

invalidation.analysis: In src/version.rs, there is no replace, resize or free operation in the module, and repository references contain no assignment to the array.
invalidation.invariant: The backing array address remains stable.

mutation_commit.analysis: In src/version.rs, the entire initialized array is installed by static initialization; readers never see a length/pointer pair being committed separately.
mutation_commit.invariant: All four version bytes are initialized before main.

release_pair.analysis: In src/version.rs, neither the exported symbol nor pointers into it may be passed to free; its owner is the loaded image for the process lifetime.
release_pair.invariant: Static image storage is never heap-released.

error_cleanup.analysis: In src/version.rs, initialization is infallible; display or parse failure does not transfer ownership of the array to its caller.
error_cleanup.invariant: Reader errors retain the original version owner.

signals_handoff.analysis: In src/version.rs, version display may run during command processing but this module installs no signal handler and performs no asynchronous writes.
signals_handoff.invariant: Current maintained users only read version storage.
limitations: The C symbol is mutable in its ABI; this review assumes maintained callers and does not certify an external writer.
